subject: Partial network isolation impacting Dedicated GPU pool — customer ops playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@orionai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Partial network isolation impacting Dedicated GPU pool — immediate mitigation

Hi Daniel —

We detected a partial network isolation affecting ~18% of your dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. Symptoms we’re seeing: a subset of nodes reporting IO stalls, elevated p95 latency from 120ms -> 900ms, and sporadic request timeouts. We kicked the automated fallback but a few job shards remained pinned to the impacted racks and didn’t migrate cleanly.

Immediate actions we’re taking now:
- Initiating manual warm-standby failover for affected tenant shards (started).
- Increasing prefix caching for your hot routes to reduce per-request IO (apply in ~5m).
- Opening a direct channel with infra to accelerate node evacuation and firmware checks (laura on-cc).

What we need from you: quick confirmation of whether you can tolerate a short burst of increased 429s during the node drain window (expected ~30–60m) and whether you want us to temporarily route all traffic to your dedicated warm standby (we can flip this for you).

I’ve attached a diagnostic snippet showing the kernel IO stalls and the runbook we’re following. I’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we stabilize.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize minimizing impact and compensating for any downtime.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: diagnostic-log-snippet.txt
From: Daniel Cho <daniel@orionai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:21:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial network isolation impacting Dedicated GPU pool — immediate mitigation

Thanks for the quick flag, Karthik.

We see the same on our side — job retries and caller-side 502s started around 09:05. Our ops dashboard shows a 3x spike in tail latency for model inference and some client-side fallbacks firing. Please go ahead and route traffic to the warm standby. We prefer short-lived rate limits over sustained errors.

One ask: can you give an ETA for full recovery and a sense of credits for the window? We’ll need a brief summary for our execs.

— Daniel
Daniel Cho
VP Infrastructure, Orion AI
ops@orionai.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial network isolation impacting Dedicated GPU pool — immediate mitigation

Team — quick ops plan:

1) Laura: confirm warm-standby routing and flip for Orion (they requested it). Add temporary rate limits at the edge (1.2x baseline) during drain.
2) Marissa: coordinate manual evacuation of impacted nodes; prioritize completing KV cache writeback then force-evict. Estimate 30–60m.
3) Stephanie: draft the external customer ETA + credit offer (Daniel asked). Use the incremental-credit template; propose 12% across the billing period and a follow-up service credit if SLA thresholds missed on re-eval.

I’m on the call with infra now. ETA for first stabilization update: +30m.

— Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@orionai.com>, Ops Team <ops@orionai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: failover initiated, recovery ETA ~3 hours; interim runbook attached

Hi Daniel / Ops —

Update: we completed the warm-standby routing flip at 09:44 PT. You should see a marked drop in tail latency; please confirm on your side. During the node evacuation we observed a transient increase in 429s (we throttled to preserve capacity) — apologies for the brief spike.

Root-cause (interim): partial network isolation between two adjacent racks (mis-synced Top-of-Rack firmware state) produced IO stalls on NVMe devices which prevented graceful eviction. Firmware logs attached in the diagnostic snippet.

Recovery plan and ETA:
- Immediate: continue manual node evacuation and reattach workloads to healthy racks (complete by ~12:30 PT).
- Short-term (24–48h): firmware patch roll and rolling power-cycling of impacted switch fabric.
- Medium-term: change routing policy to prefer cross-rack replication for critical shards (Q4 rollout).

Credit & next steps: Stephanie is preparing a formal credit offer; preliminary offer is 12% service credit applied to your next invoice, plus a technical follow-up within 48h. We’ll open a dedicated postmortem doc and share the link. Attached: dedicated-failover-runbook.pdf.

Please reply to confirm you’re back to normal or if you’re still seeing degraded tails.

Thanks for the patience — we’re keeping a high priority on this.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedicated-failover-runbook.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@orionai.com>, Ops Team <ops@orionai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & customer playbook — Orion AI dedicated pool (summary)

Daniel —

Below is a concise post-incident summary and operational playbook we’re delivering to Orion. Attaching the formal credit PDF to follow.

Incident timeline (summary)
- 09:05 PT 12 Sep: Elevated tail latency and timeouts detected; automated fallback partially triggered.
- 09:14 PT: We opened the incident with you and began manual warm-standby failover.
- 09:44 PT: Warm-standby routing flip completed; substantial recovery in p95 observed.
- 12:20 PT: Node evacuation completed for impacted racks; degraded metrics normalized.

Root cause (final)
- A firmware regression on a ToR vendor led to intermittent control-plane stalls under a specific packet rate. That caused NVMe IO queues to back up, preventing graceful eviction and leaving a subset of shards pinned.

Remediation & prevention
- Immediate: firmware patch scheduled and applied to remaining fleet; we validated with a stress test.
- Architectural: adjust shard placement to prefer cross-rack redundancy for critical routes (will reduce blast radius).
- Ops: improved detection signatures for partial isolation (synthetic probes + NVMe health heuristics).

Customer playbook (what your team can do next time)
1) Enable warm-standby routing in your account settings (we’ll pre-authorize flips for emergencies).
2) If you have client-side fallbacks, prefer short retry windows and a gradual backoff to avoid amplification.
3) Provide a single ops mailbox we can write credit and postmortem communications to (helps exec summaries).

Compensation: we’ll apply a 12% service credit for the impacted billing period and open a follow-up review with your SREs to validate mitigations. Formal credit doc: service-credit-offer-ORION-44922.pdf (attached).

Action items we own:
- Postmortem doc link (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B0-orion-runbooks
- HubSpot deal notes updated: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/HD-44922
- Ops review scheduled with Orion SREs next week (invites forthcoming).

Appreciate your partnership here — we’ll follow up with a full technical write-up and invite your team into the RCA review.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
